thread:
cs-joe: customer BlueWave reporting sharp p95/p99 latency increase on dedicated-usw2 inference pool starting ~2026-03-16T23:45Z. Multiple 504s and timeouts. customer sent traces + examples. link: https://grafana.example/bluewave/usw2
oncall-alex: thanks — assigning. which model/route? any recent infra changes in the maintenance window?
cs-joe: model: text-gen-large-v2, route: rw-dedicated-usw2-pool-7. They said last successful run ~23:30 then spike. No config change on customer side.
jordan-eng: I see an internal deploy job at 23:40 that rolled GPU firmware 3.2.1 -> 3.3.0 to a subset of nodes in pool-7. deploy-bot: "deploy job 2026-03-16T23:40 triggered: fw-rollout/gpu/3.3.0 -> pool-7 (25 nodes)"
maria-sre: interesting — our telemetry shows host-side heartbeat churn on those nodes starting 23:41. p95 for token gen jumped from ~70ms to ~420ms. kv-cache misses increased.
jordan-eng: possible pattern: new firmware increases firmware-driven telemetry heartbeat frequency, which overloads NVMe submission queue on some older hosts — looks like I/O stall cascades into GPU stall. grabbing dmesg from affected host-3. snippet:
```
[Mar 16 23:41:12] nvme0: I/O submission queue stalled, qdepth 256
[Mar 16 23:41:12] nvme0: hw timeout, recovering
[Mar 16 23:41:13] nvme0: aborting command 0x3c
[Mar 16 23:41:14] gpu0: kv cache miss spike, ioctl EIO
```
oncall-alex: can you repro locally on a node or a canary? what's safe mitigation?
jordan-eng: repro steps (do on a non-prod canary):
```
# simulate telemetry heartbeat flood
sudo ./fw_tool --stress-heartbeat --rate 2000 --device /dev/gpu0
# run p95 probe
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"text-gen-large-v2","prompt":"hello"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" | jq -r '.latency_ms'
```
maria-sre: mitigation options: 1) rollback firmware to 3.2.1 on affected nodes, 2) throttle firmware telemetry at host level (udev/sysfs knob), 3) temporarily evict/route traffic off pool-7 to pool-5 (fallback). Immediate fastest is routing and partial rollback.
oncall-alex: doing routing now — adding route rule to prefer pool-5 for BlueWave.
support-desk: ping customer that we are rerouting and investigating, will follow up in 10m. :phone:
jordan-eng: starting targeted rollback on 7 nodes showing highest nvme qdepth. patch command:
```
fwctl rollback --node host-3,host-9,host-14 --from 3.3.0 --to 3.2.1 --force
```
deploy-bot: "rollback job started: fwctl rollback -> host-3,host-9,host-14 (eta ~6m)"
maria-sre: early telemetry after routing + first 3 rollbacks: p95 dropped from 420ms -> 85ms for BlueWave, error rate down 504 -> 0.7%. still watching kv-cache miss rate.
cs-joe: customer acknowledges improvements, reports throughput back to normal for their busiest routes. they want RCA and ETA for full fix.
jordan-eng: next steps: full pool rollback plan overnight + firmware vendor engagement to root cause heartbeat rate change. I’ll open a follow-up incident with packet captures and device logs.
oncall-alex: I'll schedule automated drain + rollback for remaining impacted nodes in a controlled rolling window. will post timeline in a follow-up thread.
support-desk: relayed to customer, they want heads-up before the rest of the rollbacks. CC'ing account manager.
maria-sre: note for postmortem: add host-level guard to detect nvme qdepth > 180 and trigger temporary route fallback automatically. filing a runbook card.
cs-joe: customer closure status: "monitoring but stable". thanks team. :tada:
jordan-eng: filed bug: INFRA-12948 "fw 3.3.0 heartbeat telemetry increases NVMe qdepth on some SKUs" with logs attached.
maria-sre: closing slack thread, will consolidate in incident ticket with timelines and mitigations.
support-desk: customer asked for postmortem and ETA for vendor fix — will coordinate with eng and AM.
